claims.statement: Retained: for a rooted finite forest (G,r), attaching a pendant path of length m>=1 gives I(G_m)=I(G-r)P_m+zI(G-N[r])P_(m-1), where P_m is the m-vertex path independence polynomial. The identity computes the strict Delta_p selector at every integer rank for each surviving old original leaf tag distinct from r after attachment, and the new endpoint separately; if r was an original degree-one leaf, it is removed from the old-leaf list.
claims.scope: Exact selector evaluation under pendant-path attachment at a specified root in finite ordinary trees, for surviving original leaf tags other than a root that ceases to be a leaf, and for the new endpoint. A singleton base can create an additional root leaf not covered by this stated interface. No eligibility or primary aggregate conclusion.
claims.reason: retained — root absent/present partition proves the polynomial identity; the attachment indices, strict coefficient test, old-tag deletion interface, endpoint test, and K1,7 arithmetic check. The claim does not assert propagation of primary eligibility or S.

limitations: The recurrence establishes selector evaluation under the stated operation, not preservation of x(T), alpha(T), or the strict lower-region guard.
No bound for or verdict on the complete selected aggregate S is established.
The strict-sign example is outside primary eligibility and is not a counterexample to the primary assertion.
